title: Optimize Advisor: staged-config-apply & fast-recovery playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: This ticket captures the post-incident follow-up and operational playbook for Optimize Advisor's automated batching/caching recommendation pipeline after a mid-February rollout caused a measurable cost spike and several customer-facing tail-latency regressions. Goal: deliver a staged-config-apply flow, a lightweight preflight simulator, automatic revert heuristics, and an operator-friendly emergency rollback API so future recommendation applications are safe by default.
timeline: 2025-02-14: Initial Optimize Advisor config sweep rolled to 100% (nightly scheduled) — triggered batching increase for small-sequence workloads.
2025-02-14 02:00 UTC: Alerts: cost-per-token increase observed +12% across a subset of accounts; tail latency p95/p99 increases on models with short context lengths.
2025-02-14 02:30 UTC: On-call on duty (Liam) paused automated applies; partial manual rollback of top-5 affected customers completed by 03:10 UTC.
2025-02-15: Incident review meeting; preliminary root cause established: lacked staged canary, preflight simulation, and a cost-delta guardrail for Apply operations.
2025-02-18: This ticket opened to track engineering follow-ups and create the operator playbook.
2025-02-24: Draft of staged-apply design landed (RFC) and initial unit tests for preflight simulator added in repo.
2025-03-02: Safety runbook draft reviewed by SRE and PM; minor edits requested (add cost-health rollback thresholds).
root_cause: Optimize Advisor applied a batching profile increase globally without a phased canary or shadow validation. The advisor's delta-estimate model underestimated cache-hit regressions for short-context models. No cost-delta hard guard existed, and the automated apply lacked an automated fast-revert based on short-window anomaly detection.
mitigations: Immediate: Disable nightly global auto-applies and revert Advisor to 'suggest only' mode until staged apply exists (completed 2025-02-14).
Short-term: Add a cost-delta threshold that prevents any apply that increases per-token cost more than 5% on the sampled holdout traffic.
Short-term: Implement a 1% traffic shadow test that runs new config in shadow against production and records metric deltas for 24 hours before any rollout.
Mid-term: Create an anomaly-driven automatic revert that triggers a revert if cost or tail-latency exceed configured SLO deltas within a 30-minute sliding window.
Mid-term: Expose an operator 'force-revert' API and console action that accepts a reason and reverts the last applied config within 5 minutes.
Long-term: Integrate model-sensitive heuristics (hardware, seq-len distribution) into the Advisor's estimate model to avoid uniform increases that harm short-context workloads.
playbook_steps: 1) Detection: Alert fires when cost-per-token > baseline by configured threshold (default 7%) or when p99 latency increases by >20ms over baseline for 10m.
2) Triage: On-call reviews Advisor audit log to find latest apply bundle ID and the target cohort/models. Capture affected customers via request sampling.
3) Shadow analysis: If staged-apply was configured, inspect shadow test telemetry; if no shadow exists, escalate to SRE and set Advisor to 'suggest-only' immediately.
4) Immediate mitigation: Execute 'force-revert' for the most recent apply, or if unavailable, promote last-known-good config and restart serving processes for that cohort.
5) Communication: Notify SRE, PM, Support; open incident channel and send status updates to affected customers (template provided in docs).
6) Post-incident: Run the postmortem template, publish RCA, and schedule follow-ups for implementing missing safeguards (this ticket tracks those).
followups: (Liam O'Connor) Implement canary pipeline that escalates from 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% in 24h windows — due 2025-03-10
(Maya Patel) Enhance estimate model to incorporate seq-len distribution and cache sensitivity; first draft due 2025-03-17
(SRE Team) Add anomaly revert automation and integrate with paging playbook — due 2025-03-24
(Support) Prepare customer-facing incident templates and escalation matrix — due 2025-03-05
notes: Design decision: staged apply will default to 'opt-in' for high-risk cohorts (short-context models, low req volume) and 'opt-out' for stable cohorts.
We will gate full auto-apply re-enable on 2 weeks of stable shadow runs with zero significant cost/regression alerts.
Related: coordinate with Billing team to add per-account anomaly detection for sudden cost increases (suggested separate project).
